name: Grove Electromagnet (v1.0)
description: 5 V holding electromagnet (ZYE1-P20/15 coil, 20 mm x 15 mm, 25 N rated / about 1 kg peak hold) on a Grove board with its own low-side switch: SIG goes through 100 Ω to the gate of a CJ2302 N-channel MOSFET (100 kΩ gate pull-down), which switches the coil from VCC; a 1N4148 flyback diode sits across the coil. SIG high = magnet on, low or unconnected = off. The coil draws about 400 mA from VCC at 5 V, so feed VCC from a 5 V supply that can deliver it; a 3.3 V GPIO drives SIG directly. Sold as: Seeed Studio Grove - Electromagnet (SKU 101020073), 4-pin Grove connector SIG, NC, VCC, GND.
eli5: A magnet you can switch on and off: set the pin high and it grabs iron, set it low and it lets go.

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Control input (Grove pin 1, yellow wire): high = magnet on, low = off. Drives the CJ2302 MOSFET gate through 100 Ω, with a 100 kΩ pull-down to GND so the magnet stays off while the pin floats at boot. Draws almost no current, so a 3.3 V GPIO is enough.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Coil supply (Grove pin 3, red wire): 5 V DC at about 400 mA (Seeed spec). The whole coil current flows through this pin, so use a 5 V supply rated for at least 0.5 A with its ground shared with the microcontroller, not the board's 3V3 pin.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (Grove pin 4, black wire): MOSFET source and coil return, shared with the microcontroller and the 5 V supply.

buildNotes: Grove connector order (Seeed v1.0 Eagle schematic, J1): pin 1 SIG (yellow), pin 2 NC (white), pin 3 VCC (red), pin 4 GND (black). The board has a 2 mm Grove socket, not header pins: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable to reach the breadboard.

Circuit (Seeed v1.0 schematic): SIG → 100 Ω → CJ2302 N-MOSFET gate, 100 kΩ gate-to-GND pull-down; coil (ZYE1-P20/15, marked DC6V 0.5A) from VCC to the drain; 1N4148 flyback diode across the coil; 100 nF across VCC/GND.

Seeed spec: working voltage DC 5 V, working current 400 mA, standby current 200 µA, holds about 1 kg. Give VCC a 5 V supply good for at least 0.5 A (a USB 5 V rail can work for one magnet, but a separate 5 V supply with a common ground is safer, especially next to an ESP32's Wi-Fi current peaks).
High = hold, low = release. The 100 kΩ pull-down keeps it released while the GPIO is still floating at power-up.
The coil gets warm if left on for long periods; switch it off when not holding something. PWM on SIG (about 1 kHz) can lower the holding power once an object is held.
Holds best on flat, clean mild steel at least 5 mm thick (ZYE1-P datasheet). Thin sheet, stainless steel, aluminium and brass hold weakly or not at all.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

magnet = Pin({SIG}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # SIG high = MOSFET on = magnet holds
while True:
    magnet.value(1)
    print('MAGNET ON')
    time.sleep(2)
    magnet.value(0)
    print('MAGNET OFF')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: The electromagnet switches on, then off again
